messages:
maya: Heads-up — I saw several requests slip to fallback variants when the new 'slab' policy was active. Not sure if this is a config drift or an eval ordering bug.

axel: which routes/tenants are you seeing it on? can you paste the log snippet (redact tenant ids)?

maya: pasted logs: ```policy_id=policy.slab.v3 route=translate-us raw_score=0.42 region=eu-west1 region_penalty=0.25 final_decision=fallback``` multiple hits in last 10m.

igor: quick read: slab here = bucketized latency/cost tradeoff right? looks like region_penalty is being applied after slab assignment in the runtime.

sam: yep that's what I spotted during the perf run — slab thresholds are computed globally at load time, then region_penalty gets added later, pushing some routes into the next worse slab.

leah: that ordering would explain it. If we bucket by raw_score then add region penalty, you can oscillate across slab boundaries for noisy penalties.

axel: proposed options: (A) apply region_penalty before slab assignment (i.e. bucket on normalized_score). (B) keep current order but widen slabs so small deltas don't flip decisions. (C) compute per-region slab maps at hot-reload. Tradeoffs?

maya: A seems simplest correctness-wise, but it may change caching patterns and invalidation behavior. B is low-risk but feels like masking the real problem. C is attractive but adds memory and hot-reload complexity.

igor: C also means we have to deal with telemetry staleness: region penalties change with probes, and per-region slabs would need frequent recompute or TTLs. That increases churn on policy hot-reload.

sam: what about a hybrid: precompute a raw->slab cache and at decision time add a small delta adjustment instead of recomputing full mapping — basically: slab = lookup(raw); if (raw+penalty crosses threshold) compute fallback path, else keep cached slab. Less CPU on common path, correct on edge cases.

leah: ran a quick sim on a sample traffic slice — normalizing early (apply penalty then slab) reduced fallbacks by ~2.8% on the affected routes. But CPU microbench showed decision latency p95 +8ms under 8k qps when we recompute fully per-request.

axel: that +8ms is concerning for latency SLOs. So we need a plan that preserves p95 while reducing wrong fallbacks.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout started: policy-engine v2.1 -> 5% traffic in us-west2 (policy-slab feature flag OFF by default).

maya: action plan suggestion: 1) run the normalized-slab sim across more regions (esp. eu/asia), 2) microbenchmark the proposed hybrid approach (lookup + delta path) at target QPS, 3) add a slab-stability metric (rate of slab flips per-minute), 4) expose a per-tenant opt-out flag for slab-normalization during rollout.

igor: +1 on opt-out and the slab-stability metric. Also: keep the old behavior behind a feature-flag for rollback safety; we should not break Dedicated customers without notice.

sam: I'll draft a short RFC that (a) explains eval-order change, (b) defines the hybrid algorithm, (c) includes compatibility notes and feature-flag semantics, and (d) proposes dashboard metrics (slab_flips, fallback_rate_delta, decision_cpu_ms).

leah: small UI note — if we change semantics, Console rollout view should show a "slab normalization" toggle and display slab-flip hotspots per-route. Ops and SEs will ask for that.

maya: cool. I'll hold the larger canary until we have sim + microbench results. ping me with artifacts and perf numbers.

axel: thanks, team. I'll schedule a 30m follow-up after Sam posts the RFC. :thumbsup:
